examples.en: New members are warmly welcome anytime.

examples.ko: 동네 사람들이 새로 온 의사 선생님을 대환영했어요.
examples.en: The neighbors gave the new doctor a big welcome.
Everyone is welcome, so come without worrying.
The atmosphere was so welcoming that I settled in quickly.
Good ideas will always be warmly welcomed.
I was so grateful that the guests welcomed me so warmly.

explain: '환영하다'보다 훨씬 반기는 느낌이 강하고 말투도 친근해요. 모집 글이나 가게 문구에서 '대환영이에요'처럼 명사로도 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: Beginners are very welcome too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모집 글이나 가게 문구에서 명사처럼 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used like a noun in recruitment posts and shop signs.

phrases.en: My friends gave me a big welcome.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 크게 반겨 주었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone greeted you with a warm, big welcome.

phrases.en: I received a big welcome in my hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반겨 주는 쪽이 아니라 반김을 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person being welcomed.

explain_en: It sounds much more enthusiastic than '환영하다' and has a friendly tone. In recruitment posts and shop signs you often see the noun form, like '대환영이에요'.

examples.en: We are the same age, so we talk casually.
A friend my age joined the company.
Gathered with people the same age, we get along well.

examples.ko: 우리 동갑이에요? 저도 같은 해에 태어났어요.
examples.en: Are we the same age? I was born in the same year too.
I have many friends my age, so I am not lonely.
My cousin is my age, so we are in the same class.

explain: 한국에서는 나이에 따라 말투가 달라져서 동갑인지 먼저 물어보는 경우가 있어요. 동갑이면 말을 놓자고 하기도 해요. 나이가 많으면 '연상', 어리면 '연하'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I went on a trip with a friend my age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이가 같은 사람을 친근하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly word for someone of the same age.

phrases.example: 우리 동갑이야? 그럼 말 편하게 하자.
phrases.en: Are we the same age? Then let's speak casually.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 편한 사이에서 반말로 물어볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual question used with friends or people you are close to.

phrases.en: I'm glad to have many friends my age.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동갑'을 명사 앞에 붙여서 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 동갑 can be placed before a noun.

explain_en: In Korea speech style changes with age, so people sometimes first ask if you are the same age. If you are, they may suggest dropping formal speech. Someone older is '연상' and someone younger is '연하'.

examples.en: A weekend alone is really boring.
Today's class was so boring.
The dull talk went on for a long while.

examples.ko: 할 일이 없으면 하루가 따분할 거예요.
examples.en: If you have nothing to do, the day will be dull.
Shall we play a game together so it is not boring?

examples.ko: 비가 와서 밖에도 못 나가니까 따분해서 죽겠어요.
examples.en: It is raining and I cannot go out, so I am bored to death.

explain: '심심하다', '지루하다'와 비슷해요. '심심하다'는 할 일이 없을 때 주로 쓰고, '따분하다'는 '따분한 이야기', '따분한 사람'처럼 재미없는 대상을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: That teacher's stories are a bit boring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따분한'을 명사 앞에 붙여서 재미없는 대상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 따분한 before a noun to describe a boring thing.

phrases.en: I was so bored that I watched a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따분한 이유로 다음 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to give boredom as the reason for what you did.

phrases.en: This book isn't boring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재미없지 않다고 말할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying something is not boring.

explain_en: It is close to '심심하다' and '지루하다'. '심심하다' is mainly for when you have nothing to do, while '따분하다' can also describe a dull thing, as in '따분한 이야기' and '따분한 사람'.

examples.en: There are many old records in Grandpa's room.
When you play a record, a warm sound comes out.

examples.ko: 중고 가게에서 레코드판을 한 장 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a record at a used shop.

examples.ko: 요즘 레코드판을 모으는 젊은 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: These days there are young people who collect records.
Dust has built up on the record, so the sound skips.
I carefully put the needle on the record.

explain: 바늘로 소리를 읽는 둥근 음반이에요. 'LP판'이라고도 하고, CD까지 포함하는 넓은 말은 '음반'이에요. 옛날 물건이라는 느낌이 있어서 추억 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My father likes collecting LP records.
phrases.nuance_ko: 레코드판과 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 레코드판.

phrases.en: I collect old records.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취미를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about hobbies.

phrases.en: There is a small record shop in my neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가게'를 붙여 레코드판을 파는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 가게 (shop) shows the place that sells records.

explain_en: It is the round disc played with a needle. It is also called 'LP판', and the broader word that includes CDs is '음반'. It carries an old-time feeling and often appears in nostalgic talk.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 전반전에 두 골 리드를 잡았어요.
examples.en: Our team took a two-goal lead in the first half.

examples.ko: 기사의 리드만 읽어도 내용을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get the story just by reading the lead of the article.
We lost the lead at the last moment.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 처음부터 끝까지 리드를 놓치지 않았어요.
examples.en: That player never gave up the lead from start to finish.

examples.ko: 리드가 좋은 기사는 첫 문장부터 눈길을 끌어요.
examples.en: An article with a good lead catches your eye from the first sentence.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 리드 기타가 정말 멋있어요.
examples.en: The lead guitar in this song is really cool.

explain: 경기에서 앞서 있는 상태도 '리드', 기사의 맨 앞 문단도 '리드'라고 해요. 동사로는 '리드하다'를 쓰고, 같은 뜻의 순우리말은 '앞서다'예요. 점수를 말할 때는 '리드를 잡다', '리드를 지키다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Our team is leading the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '리드'를 동사로 써서 앞서 가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 리드, describing being ahead.

phrases.en: We held the one-goal lead in the second half too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞선 점수를 끝까지 유지할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when keeping a lead until the end.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 한 골 앞서고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our team is ahead by one goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '리드'와 같은 뜻의 순우리말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word with the same meaning as 리드.

explain_en: '리드' covers being ahead in a game and the opening paragraph of a news article. The native Korean word for being ahead is '앞서다'. For scores, the set phrases are '리드를 잡다' (take the lead) and '리드를 지키다' (hold the lead). As a verb it is '리드하다'.

examples.en: I put on mascara to make my eyes look bigger.
I got rained on, so my mascara smudged.

examples.ko: 이 마스카라는 물에 잘 안 지워져요.
examples.en: This mascara does not wash off easily with water.

examples.ko: 가방 안에 마스카라와 립스틱이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: There is mascara and lipstick in my bag.
My eyes sting because of the mascara.
I bought new mascara and lotion too.

explain: 화장품은 보통 '바르다'와 같이 써서 '마스카라를 바르다'라고 해요. 마스카라는 속눈썹에 바르고, 눈 가장자리에 선을 그리는 '아이라인'은 '그리다'를 써요. 지울 때는 '지우다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I put on mascara in the morning and went out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마스카라를 쓸 때 가장 자주 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb for putting on mascara.

phrases.en: I always remove my mascara before I sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장을 없앨 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking off makeup.

phrases.en: I often use black mascara.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마스카라의 색을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the color of mascara.

explain_en: Makeup usually goes with '바르다', so you say '마스카라를 바르다'. Mascara goes on the eyelashes, but drawing a line along the eye, '아이라인', uses '그리다'. To take it off you use '지우다'.

examples.en: On April Fool's Day, my friend lied to me.
Tomorrow is April 1st, April Fool's Day.
Since it was April Fool's Day, I sent a text as a joke.
I was completely fooled by my friend's April Fool's lie.
What are you going to do this April Fool's Day?

examples.ko: 만우절 때 선생님이 농담을 하셔서 다 같이 웃었어요.
examples.en: On April Fool's Day our teacher made a joke, and we all laughed together.

explain: '만우절 거짓말', '만우절 장난'처럼 짝을 이뤄 자주 써요. 4월 1일이지만 쉬는 날은 아니에요. 가볍게 장난치는 날이라서 심한 거짓말은 하지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: I was completely fooled by my friend's April Fool's lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만우절'과 짝을 이뤄 자주 쓰는 말로, 4월 1일에 하는 가벼운 거짓말을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for the harmless lies people tell on April 1st.

phrases.example: 동료가 만우절 장난으로 제 의자를 숨겼어요.
phrases.en: A coworker hid my chair as an April Fool's prank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거짓말뿐 아니라 행동으로 하는 장난까지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for pranks done through actions, not only for lies.

phrases.example: 오늘은 만우절이라서 뉴스를 그냥 믿을 수가 없어요.
phrases.en: Since today is April Fool's Day, I can't just believe the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-이라서'를 붙여 오늘 일어난 일의 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-이라서' lets you give April Fool's Day as the reason for something.

explain_en: It pairs with words as in '만우절 거짓말' and '만우절 장난'. It falls on April 1st, but it is not a day off. It is a day for light pranks, so it's better not to tell serious lies.

examples.en: The telephone was invented in the 19th century.
With the invention of a new machine, life became easier.
They say paper was invented a very long time ago.
I do not know when this tool was invented.

examples.ko: 발명된 물건 중에서 가장 유용한 게 뭐예요?
examples.en: Of all the things invented, which is the most useful?
Many things are invented out of need.

explain: 새로 만들어 낸 물건이나 방법에 써요. 원래 있던 것을 처음 찾아낼 때는 '발견되다'를 써서 구별해요. 능동은 '발명하다', 사람은 '발명가'예요.

phrases.en: He invented a new machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만든 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the inventor as subject.

phrases.en: He is a famous inventor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발명을 하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who invents.

phrases.en: A new star was discovered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 있던 것을 처음 찾을 때 써서 '발명되다'와 구별해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for finding something that already existed, unlike 발명되다.

explain_en: It is used for newly made things and methods. For something that already existed and was found for the first time, use '발견되다' (be discovered). The active form is '발명하다' and a person who does it is a '발명가' (inventor).

examples.en: The child scoops up rice with a small spoon.

examples.ko: 동생은 말없이 밥숟가락을 들었지만 밥은 반도 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling silently picked up the spoon but couldn't finish even half the rice.
Could you give me one more spoon, please?

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 밥숟가락 들 힘도 없어요.
examples.en: I'm so tired I don't even have the strength to lift a spoon.

examples.ko: 할머니는 밥숟가락 위에 김치를 올려 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother put kimchi on top of my spoonful of rice.

examples.ko: 밥숟가락이 바닥에 떨어져서 큰 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: The spoon fell on the floor and made a loud noise.

explain: '숟가락'은 모든 숟가락을 가리키고, '밥숟가락'은 밥 먹을 때 쓰는 큰 숟가락이라서 작은 '찻숟가락'과 구별할 때 써요. 일상에서는 보통 그냥 '숟가락'이라고 해요. 숟가락과 젓가락을 합쳐서 '수저'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I feed the baby rice with a spoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모든 숟가락을 가리키는 더 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general word for any spoon.

phrases.en: Please set the spoons and chopsticks on the table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숟가락과 젓가락을 합쳐 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for a spoon and chopsticks together.

phrases.en: I was hungry, so I quickly picked up my spoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥을 먹기 시작한다는 뜻으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can also mean starting to eat a meal.

explain_en: '숟가락' means any spoon, while '밥숟가락' is the larger spoon for eating rice, used to tell it apart from the small '찻숟가락' (teaspoon). In daily life people usually just say '숟가락'. A spoon and chopsticks together are also called '수저'.

examples.en: This is no big deal, so do not worry.

examples.ko: 우리는 별거도 아닌 일로 크게 싸웠어요.
examples.en: We had a big fight over nothing much.

examples.ko: 오늘은 별거 안 하고 집에서 쉬었어요.
examples.en: Today I didn't do anything special and rested at home.
It is nothing special, but please enjoy it.
That store has all sorts of things.
Why brag so much as if this is such a big deal?

explain: '별것'을 말할 때 줄인 말이에요. '별거 아니에요'는 선물이나 도움에 대해 고맙다는 말을 들었을 때 낮추어 답하는 표현이기도 해요. 같은 소리의 '별거'(別居)는 부부가 따로 사는 것이라 다른 단어예요.

phrases.en: It's nothing; no big deal
phrases.nuance_ko: 고맙다는 말에 낮춰 답하거나 쉽다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to reply humbly to thanks or to say something is easy.

explain_en: It is the spoken short form of '별것'. '별거 아니에요' is also a humble reply when someone thanks you for a gift or help. The same-sounding '별거' (別居, living apart) is a different word.

examples.en: I felt bad going empty-handed, so I bought some fruit.
The hunter came home empty-handed.
The child held out an empty hand and smiled.
I put a warm coffee into his empty hand.
He opened the door with nothing in his hands.
It is fine to come empty-handed, so just bring yourself.

explain: '빈손으로 오다', '빈손으로 가다'처럼 '-으로'와 함께 써요. 아무것도 들지 않은 손이 '빈손'이고, 장갑이나 도구 없이 있는 그대로의 손은 '맨손'이에요.

phrases.en: It's fine if you come empty-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선물이나 물건 없이 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when coming without a gift or things.

phrases.en: He left the house empty-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무것도 들지 않고 나갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when leaving without carrying anything.

phrases.en: I couldn't buy anything, so I went back empty-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하는 것을 얻지 못하고 돌아갈 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when you return without getting what you wanted.

explain_en: It goes with '-으로', as in '빈손으로 오다' and '빈손으로 가다'. A '빈손' is a hand holding nothing, while a '맨손' is a bare hand without gloves or tools.

examples.en: This app is used all over the world.
This room used to be used as a meeting room.

examples.ko: 이 도구는 요리할 때만 사용되는 것이 아니에요.
examples.en: This tool isn't used only when cooking.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 편지에서 자주 사용돼서 알아 두면 좋아요.
examples.en: This word is often used in letters, so it's good to know.

examples.ko: 앞으로 이 건물은 도서관으로 사용될 거예요.
examples.en: From now on, this building will be used as a library.

examples.ko: 버려지지 않고 다시 사용되면 환경에 좋아요.
examples.en: If things are reused instead of thrown away, it's good for the environment.

explain: '사용하다'는 사람이 쓰는 것이고, '사용되다'는 쓰이는 물건이나 말이 주어예요. 설명서·뉴스·보고서에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '쓰여요'(쓰이다)를 더 많이 써요. 도구·말·돈에는 '사용', 시설·서비스에는 '이용'이 어울려요.

phrases.en: This word is often used in daily life.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사용되다'와 같은 뜻이에요. 말할 때는 '쓰이다'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 사용되다; 쓰이다 is more common in speech.

phrases.en: This app is widely used in schools.
phrases.nuance_ko: '널리'를 붙이면 많은 곳에서 쓰인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 널리 means it is used in many places.

phrases.en: That room is not being used now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여 쓰이지 않는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -지 않다 to say it is not in use.

explain_en: '사용하다' is a person using something; with '사용되다' the thing or word being used is the subject. You see it in manuals, news and reports. In speech, '쓰여요' (쓰이다) is more common. Use '사용' for tools, words and money, and '이용' for facilities and services.

p.n: 쓰이다 is a more everyday, spoken-sounding word.

examples.en: My brother is quiet, but I am a chatterbox.
My friend is an incurable chatterbox.

examples.ko: 수다쟁이 동생 덕분에 집이 늘 시끌시끌해요.
examples.en: Thanks to my chatty younger sibling, the house is always noisy.

examples.ko: 우리 반 수다쟁이가 오늘은 웬일로 조용해요.
examples.en: For some reason, the chatterbox of our class is quiet today.

examples.ko: 수다쟁이 할머니가 이웃 이야기를 다 알고 계세요.
examples.en: The chatty grandmother knows all the stories about the neighbors.

examples.ko: 저는 원래 수다쟁이가 아닌데 그 사람 앞에서는 말이 많아져요.
examples.en: I am not normally a chatterbox, but I talk a lot in front of that person.

explain: '멋쟁이', '고집쟁이'처럼 '-쟁이'가 붙은 말이라 친근하거나 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 윗사람에게 직접 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요. 성격을 부드럽게 말할 때는 '말이 많다', '수다스럽다'를 써요.

phrases.en: When I meet my friends, I become a chatterbox.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특정한 사람 앞에서 말이 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you talk a lot around certain people.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is chatty, so the house is noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 직접 놀리는 느낌이 적어서 더 부드럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels less like teasing, so it sounds gentler.

phrases.example: 저는 친한 친구 앞에서는 말이 많아요.
phrases.en: I talk a lot in front of close friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격이나 상황을 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to casually describe a personality or situation.

explain_en: Like '멋쟁이' and '고집쟁이', the '-쟁이' ending gives it a friendly or teasing tone. It can be rude to use directly about someone older. For a softer description, say '말이 많다' or '수다스럽다'.

examples.en: Who is it this round?
I lost at rock-paper-scissors, so I became the seeker.
The seeker closes their eyes and counts to ten.
Hide quickly so the seeker doesn't catch you!
My younger sibling grumbles that they don't want to be it all the time.
We played rock-paper-scissors to decide who would be it.

explain: '술래가 되다', '술래를 정하다'처럼 써요. 숨바꼭질에서는 찾는 사람이고, 얼음땡 같은 놀이에서는 쫓아가는 사람이에요.

phrases.en: We decide who is it by rock-paper-scissors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이를 시작하기 전에 술래를 뽑을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a game to choose who is it.

phrases.en: I'll be it this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '술래가 되다'보다 자기가 하겠다고 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 술래가 되다 when volunteering.

phrases.en: If you get caught, we switch who is it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡힌 사람이 술래가 되는 규칙을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the rule that the caught player becomes it.

explain_en: It is used as '술래가 되다' (to be it) or '술래를 정하다' (to choose who is it). In hide-and-seek it is the one who searches, and in games like freeze tag it is the chaser.

examples.en: I am right-handed, but my younger sibling is left-handed.
These scissors are for right-handed people, so they're awkward for me.
If a right-hander writes with the left hand, the writing gets crooked.
Everyone in my family is right-handed.
I'm right-handed, so my right shoulder often hurts.
Most tools are made to suit right-handed people.

explain: 반대말은 '왼손잡이'이고, 손이 아니라 그런 사람을 가리켜요. 도구 이름 뒤에 '용'을 붙여 '오른손잡이용'이라고 하면 오른손잡이를 위해 만든 물건이에요.

phrases.en: This mouse is for right-handed people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 이름 앞에 붙여서 오른손잡이를 위해 만든 것이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before an item to mean it is made for right-handers.

phrases.en: I'm right-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 어느 손을 주로 쓰는지 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which hand you mainly use.

phrases.en: There are many right-handed people in our class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수를 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing numbers of people.

explain_en: The opposite is '왼손잡이'. It refers to the person, not the hand itself. Adding '용' as in '오른손잡이용' means something made for right-handed people.

examples.en: Please don't misunderstand what I said.
My friend completely misunderstood me.
People often misunderstand this word.
I'll explain in detail so there's no misunderstanding.
I'm sorry I misheard and misunderstood.
If you misunderstood my text message, I'm sorry.

explain: 사람의 마음이나 말을 잘못 받아들였을 때 써요. 명사 '오해'로 '오해를 풀다', '오해를 사다'처럼 쓰는 일도 많아요. '오해하지 마세요'는 아주 자주 쓰는 표현이라 통째로 외워 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: Please don't misunderstand me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 자주 쓰는 표현이라 통째로 외워 두면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common expression worth memorizing as a whole.

phrases.en: I met my friend and cleared up the misunderstanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못 알았던 일을 바로잡을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for correcting a misunderstanding.

phrases.en: I misunderstood that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 잘못 받아들인 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for having taken something the wrong way.

explain_en: Use it when you take someone's feelings or words the wrong way. The noun '오해' is also common in '오해를 풀다' (clear up a misunderstanding) and '오해를 사다' (be misunderstood). '오해하지 마세요' is a very common expression, so it is worth memorizing as a whole.

examples.ko: 이다음에 시간 되면 또 같이 와요.
examples.en: Let's come again together next time when we have time.
You can get off at the next stop.
Next is my turn to present.
Next time I'll make sure not to be late.
I'm worried about what comes next and I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 이다음 주에는 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like it will rain the week after this.

explain: '이다음에'는 '나중에, 훗날'처럼 막연한 앞날이나 다음 기회를 말할 때 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '다음에'나 '나중에'도 많이 써요. 순서를 말할 때는 '이다음 정류장'처럼 바로 뒤의 것을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: Let's go on a trip together sometime later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막연한 앞날의 기회를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a vague future opportunity.

phrases.en: I'll get off at the next stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 뒤에 오는 것을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Points to the one coming right after this.

phrases.en: Let's talk again later.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다음에'와 비슷하고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '이다음에' and more common in daily speech.

explain_en: '이다음에' is often used for a vague future or the next chance, like 'later' or 'someday'. In daily talk '다음에' and '나중에' are also common. For order, it points to the one right after this, as in '이다음 정류장' (the stop after this).

examples.en: Hey, what do you think you're doing?
The boss called out, 'Hey, Assistant Manager Kim!'
In the drama, he shouted, 'Hey! Stop right there!'

examples.ko: 아저씨가 '이봐 학생' 하고 저를 불러 세웠어요.
examples.en: A man called out 'Hey, student' and stopped me.

examples.ko: '이봐, 이봐!' 하고 누가 저를 계속 불러요.
examples.en: Someone keeps calling me, 'Hey, hey!'

examples.ko: 옛날 영화에서는 '이봐, 친구' 하고 말을 거는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: In old movies there are scenes where someone says, 'Hey, pal.'

explain: 친구나 아랫사람을 부를 때 쓰는 말투라서, 윗사람이나 처음 보는 어른에게 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요. 낯선 사람을 정중하게 부를 때는 '저기요'를 써요.

phrases.example: 이봐요, 여기서 담배 피우면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Hey, you can't smoke here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이봐'보다 조금 공손하지만 낯선 사람에게는 여전히 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more polite than '이봐', but can still sound rough to strangers.

phrases.en: Excuse me, could you tell me the way?
phrases.nuance_ko: 낯선 사람이나 어른을 정중하게 부를 때 써서 '이봐'보다 안전해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to call a stranger or an elder, safer than '이봐'.

phrases.en: My friend called me, saying 'Hey, wait a second!'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 상대를 멈추게 하려고 짧게 덧붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short add-on between close friends to make someone stop.

explain_en: It is used to call a friend or someone younger or lower in rank, so with an elder or a stranger it can sound rude. To politely get a stranger's attention, use '저기요'.

examples.ko: 동생은 주말마다 열두 시까지 자는 잠꾸러기예요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a sleepyhead who sleeps until noon every weekend.
I'm a sleepyhead, so I'm always late for morning appointments.
My son is a sleepyhead, so he's hard to wake up.
Hey sleepyhead, get up now!

examples.ko: 저는 잠꾸러기가 아니고 밤에 일하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: I'm not a sleepyhead, I'm someone who works at night.
I found out after marriage that my husband is a sleepyhead.

explain: 잠이 많은 사람을 귀엽게 놀릴 때 써요. 아이나 가까운 사이에 쓰고, 어른에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요. '장난꾸러기', '욕심꾸러기'처럼 '-꾸러기'가 붙은 말도 있어요.

phrases.en: My sleepyhead little brother overslept again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이나 가까운 사람 앞에 붙여서 귀엽게 놀리는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before a family member or close person to tease them in a cute way.

phrases.en: My friend teases me by calling me a sleepyhead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠이 많은 사람을 장난스럽게 놀릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when playfully teasing someone who sleeps a lot.
phrases.en_equiv: to tease someone as a sleepyhead

phrases.en: My son is a total sleepyhead.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전'을 붙이면 잠이 아주 많다는 뜻이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '완전' makes it stronger: the person sleeps a lot.

explain_en: It is used to tease someone affectionately for sleeping a lot. Use it with children or close people; saying it directly to an adult can be rude. Other words with '-꾸러기' include '장난꾸러기' and '욕심꾸러기'.

examples.en: A west-facing living room is nice because the evening glow is beautiful.
I walked along the riverside watching the sunset glow.
The sky was dyed red by the evening glow.
We took photos under the evening glow.

examples.ko: 저녁노을은 날씨가 맑은 날 더 예뻐요.
examples.en: The evening glow is prettier on clear days.
The evening glow is settling over the sea.

explain: '노을'만 써도 되고, '저녁노을'은 해가 질 때라는 점을 분명히 해요. 아침에 보이는 노을은 '아침노을'이라고 해요. '노을이 지다', '노을이 물들다'가 어울리는 짝이에요.

phrases.en: The sunset glow in the sky is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저녁노을'보다 짧고, 시간대를 따로 말하지 않아도 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than '저녁노을', and used when you don't need to say the time of day.

phrases.en: I watched the sea as the evening glow set.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 질 때 하늘이 붉어지는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes the sky turning red as the sun sets.

phrases.en: The sky dyed with the evening glow was really beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하늘의 색을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe the color of the sky.
phrases.en_equiv: sky tinted by the evening glow

explain_en: '노을' alone is fine; '저녁노을' makes clear it is at sunset. The glow seen in the morning is '아침노을'. Natural pairings are '노을이 지다' and '노을이 물들다'.

examples.en: In summer, thin pants are cool and comfortable.

examples.ko: 이 쇼핑몰은 팬츠 종류가 정말 다양해요.
examples.en: This online store has a really wide variety of pants.

examples.ko: 검은 팬츠에 흰 셔츠를 입고 면접에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the interview in black pants and a white shirt.

examples.ko: 키가 작아서 팬츠 길이를 줄여야 해요.
examples.en: I am short, so I need to shorten the length of my pants.

examples.ko: 운동할 때는 잘 늘어나는 팬츠를 입어요.
examples.en: When I work out, I wear pants that stretch well.

examples.ko: 그 가게에서 팬츠 두 벌을 사면 한 벌은 할인해 줘요.
examples.en: If you buy two pairs of pants at that shop, one is discounted.

explain: 가게나 상품 이름에서는 '팬츠'를 많이 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 보통 '바지'라고 해요. '팬티'는 속옷이라서 서로 바꿔 쓰면 안 돼요.

phrases.en: I wore comfortable pants today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '팬츠'와 같은 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '바지'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 팬츠; 바지 is more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: Wide-leg pants are nice and cool in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통이 넓은 바지예요. 옷 가게나 쇼핑몰에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pants with a wide leg, often seen in shops and online stores.

phrases.en: I wear sweatpants when I exercise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동할 때 입는 편한 바지예요. '운동복 바지'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Comfortable pants for exercise, like sweatpants or track pants; also called '운동복 바지'.

explain_en: Shops and product names often use '팬츠', while everyday speech usually says '바지'. '팬티' means underwear, so the two cannot be swapped.

examples.en: I took out a sledgehammer to break a big rock.
This hammer is much heavier than I expected.
My hand hurt after hitting the wall with a hammer.
The nail struck by the hammer went in deep.
Both the hammer and the screwdriver are in the toolbox.

examples.ko: 육상 대회에서 해머 던지기 경기를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the hammer throw event at the athletics meet.

explain: '해머'는 크고 무거운 망치예요. 보통 망치는 '망치'라고 해요. 육상 종목 '해머던지기'에서도 '해머'를 써요.

phrases.en: I hit the wall with a hammer and broke it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 무거운 망치로 세게 칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for hitting hard with a big, heavy hammer.

phrases.en: The hammer throw is a track and field event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 종목 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of an athletic event.

phrases.en: He lifted the heavy hammer with ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무거운 해머를 손에 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for lifting a heavy hammer by hand.

explain_en: 해머 is a big, heavy hammer. An ordinary hammer is called 망치. In the track-and-field event 해머던지기, 해머 is also the word used.

examples.en: If you follow the arrows, you will reach the exit.
The arrow drawn on the road points to the right.
I move through the menu with the arrow keys on the keyboard.
I marked the route on the map with a red arrow.
What does this arrow mean?
If you touch the arrow, the screen moves on.

explain: 방향을 알려 주는 '→' 모양을 가리켜요. '화살표를 따라가다', '화살표로 표시하다'처럼 말해요. '느낌표', '물음표'처럼 '-표'로 끝나는 부호 이름이기도 해요.

phrases.en: I marked the road with an arrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방향이나 위치를 그림으로 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing a direction or place with a drawing.

phrases.en: Please walk in the direction of the arrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 길을 알려 줄 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in signs and directions.

phrases.en: If you press the up arrow, it goes up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터나 기계의 화살표 버튼을 누를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pressing arrow buttons on a computer or machine.

explain_en: It names the → shape that shows direction. You say 화살표를 따라가다 or 화살표로 표시하다. Like 느낌표 and 물음표, it ends in -표, the suffix for a sign or mark.
